tools.name: search_projects
tools.description: Search the notavibe catalog of open-source projects. The query matches project name, project description, and the category, ecosystem, kind, runtime, license_family and capabilities vocabulary facets; free-form repository topics are not matched. capabilities names what a project does, such as http-c

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Return the public profile of one catalog project, identified either by host and an owner/repo slug or a numeric repository id, or by registry and package, a package name on a package registry. host and exactly one of slug or id are required unless registry and package are given; a call missing them,

tools.name: compare_projects
tools.description: Return the public profiles of two catalog projects side by side, identified by host and two owner/repo slugs; a former slug resolves as it does for get_project. The response presents each project's facts and hhealth bands; it draws no conclusion and names no winner. What each band means is published

tools.name: get_lists
tools.description: List the public curated lists in the notavibe catalog, or return the public members of one list identified by owner handle and list slug. Only public lists and their publishable members are returned; a list that does not exist or is not public returns {"found": false, "subject": "list"}. handle and

tools.name: get_methodology
tools.description: Return what each of the catalog's five health signals measures and, for each signal, its bands in order, each with a one-line meaning and its published cut-point. The text is the same as the catalog's methodology page (/methodology), built from the same source. Takes no arguments. Reads no catalog d

tools.name: check_dependencies
tools.description: Look up a list of package names on one package registry and return one row per name, in the order given, so the health of a project's dependencies can be read in one call. ecosystem is the package registry the names belong to and accepts only the package registries this catalog admits, currently npm

tools.name: get_more_tools
tools.description: Records a description of a capability missing from the other tools of this server, for the maintainers of this server. The description is stored by an analytics service. It returns an acknowledgement and adds no tools: every tool of this server is already listed. Reads no catalog data. Serves catalo

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_project, check_dependencies · Private data: search_projects, get_project, check_dependencies, get_more_tools · Public sink: get_project · Destructive: get_project.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_project, check_dependencies · Private data: search_projects, get_project, check_dependencies, get_more_tools · Public sink: get_project · Destructive: get_project

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_projects" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
